'''Klaus Rüdenberg''' (born August 25, 1920)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iaqms.org/members/ruedenberg.php|title=Klaus Ruedenberg|work=IAQMS|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref> is a German-born American [[chemist]].

== Life and career ==
Ruedenberg was born in [[Bielefeld]], the son of Otto Rüdenberg and Meta Sophie Wertheimer. His father was [[Jews|Jewish]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Aus einer Hochburg des Reformjudentums. Quellensammlung zum Bielefelder Judentum des 19. und 20. Jahrhunderts|pages=235–236|first=Monika|last=Minninger|date=2006|publisher=Bielefeld|language=German}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Fribourg]], earning his [[Master of Science|MS degree]] in [[chemistry]] and [[mathematics]]. He also attended the [[University of Zurich]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[theoretical physics]]. After earning his degrees, he worked as a research associate with [[Robert S. Mulliken]] at the [[University of Chicago]] from 1950 to 1955.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.iastate.edu/people/klaus-ruedenberg|title=Dr. Klaus Ruedenberg|work=[[Iowa State University]]|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref>

Ruedenberg served as a professor in the department of the [[Johns Hopkins University]] from 1962 to 1964. During his years as a professor, in 1962, Ruedenberg was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=klaus%20ruedenberg&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref> After his professorship at Hopkins, he served as a professor in the same department at [[Iowa State University]] from 1964 to 1991. During his years as a professor, in 1978, he was named a [[distinguished professor]],<ref name="c">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.iastate.edu/files/people/cv/prof._cv_k_ruedenberg.pdf|title=Professional Curriculum Vitae of Klaus Ruedenberg|work=[[Iowa State University]]|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref> and in 1980, he was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic?field_last_name_value=All&field_address_city=All&field_address_when_elected_administrative_area=All&field_address_when_elected_country_code=All&field_year_elected=&field_primary_aaas_section=All&field_status_value=All&field_year_status_changed_value=&name_combine=ruedenberg&field_institutional_affiliation_value=|title=Historic Fellows|work=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref>

In 2005, Ruedenberg was named an honorary member of the [[International Academy of Mathematical Chemistry]].<ref name="c" />

== Personal life ==
In 1948, Ruedenberg married Veronika Kutter. Their marriage lasted until her death in 2004.<ref>{{Citation|title=Who's who in the Midwest: A Biographical Dictionary of Noteworthy Men and Women of the Central and Midwestern States|page=504|publisher=Marquis Who's Who, LLC}}</ref>

On August 25, 2020, Ruedenberg [[Centenarian|turned 100]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ameslab.gov/news/happy-birthday-klaus|title=Happy 100th Birthday, Klaus!|work=AMES National Laboratory|date=August 25, 2020|access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref>
